holidays.name: National Limerick Day
holidays.description: A day for rhyming silliness. Write a cheeky five-line poem with a bouncy AABBA rhyme scheme and read it aloud to anyone who will listen. The sillier and naughtier the punchline, the better.
holidays.origin: The day marks the birthday of Edward Lear, born May 12, 1812. Lear was an English artist and writer who made the limerick famous through his 1846 'Book of Nonsense'.
holidays.funFact: Lear never called his poems limericks. The name was attached to the form only after his death, and its link to the Irish city of Limerick is still debated.

holidays.name: National Odometer Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble gadget that tells you how far you've gone. Check your dashboard, admire your mileage, and maybe plan a road trip to roll those numbers over.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, usually tied to the history of early distance-measuring devices. It's a nod to the instrument that turned every drive into a number you can brag about.
holidays.funFact: Ancient Roman engineers described a cart-wheel device that dropped a pebble into a container for every mile traveled. It was an early ancestor of the modern odometer.

holidays.name: National Nutty Fudge Day
holidays.description: An excuse to eat rich, chocolatey fudge packed with crunchy nuts. Whip up a batch with walnuts, pecans, or almonds, or just grab a square and enjoy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a yearly favorite on May 12 for people with a sweet tooth.
holidays.funFact: Fudge is often said to have started as a candy-making mistake. The story goes that a batch of caramels went wrong, and the soft, creamy result was called 'fudge'.
